metadata.note: The one boundary that leaves this package is KvRedisExecutor.execute(command). It is expressed here over the REST transport, because that is the shape an HTTP-fronted store actually receives; a RESP or in-process adapter satisfies the same expectations with the same bodies. The load-bearing rule is the second interaction: a rejected command is a returned error reply, never a thrown exception, because several conformance cases assert that a command MUST be rejected and a throw makes those indistinguishable from a broken socket.

interactions.description: a command is a verb followed by arguments that reach the store byte-for-byte
a rejected command is an error reply, not a thrown exception

body.message: ERR value is not an integer or out of range

interactions.description: nil is a null value reply and is distinct from the empty string
an integer reply may arrive as a numeric string; TTL over REST and over RESP legitimately differ here
a value over the declared maximum is refused rather than silently truncated
a transport failure is not a store answer: the runner aborts the run rather than recording a case result
